extracted.intended_audience: NCPC staff, FOIA/Privacy Act program officials, and FOIA/Privacy Act requesters
extracted.subtask_short: FOIA and Privacy Act compliance guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Agency regulations describing NCPC procedures for assessing and charging FOIA fees, fee waiver standards, record preservation, and implementing the Privacy Act (program responsibilities, definitions, record-keeping, notice, SORN, and safeguards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester categorization for fee assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall categorize Requesters into three categories: Commercial Use Requesters; Noncommercial Scientific Institutions, Educational Institutions, and News Media Requesters; and all other Requesters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different fees shall be charged depending upon the category into which a Requester falls. If fees apply, a Requester may seek a fee waiver in accordance with § 602.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee exemption for educational, noncommercial scientific, and news media requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall not charge Search fees to Requests made by Educational Institutions, Noncommercial Scientific Institutions, or Representatives of the News Media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC shall charge Search fees to all other Requesters subject to restrictions even if NCPC fails to locate any responsive Records or withholds Records based on a FOIA exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee calculation and hourly rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Search fees for each quarter hour spent searching Records are calculated based on the average hourly GS base salary plus DC locality payment plus 16% for benefits for three personnel categories: Staff Assistant (GS 9–11), Professional Personnel (GS 11–13), Managerial Staff (GS 14–15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarter-hour fees specified: Staff Assistant $9.00; Professional Personnel $12.00; Managerial Personnel $18.00 per quarter hour. Applies to searches including electronic searches that do not require new programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer search direct cost charging
rubrics_metrics.description: For a computer Search of Records, Requesters shall be charged the Direct Costs of creating a computer program, if necessary, and/or conducting the Search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct Costs include costs directly attributable to the Search and the operator’s salary for time attributable to the Search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplication fees shall be charged to all Requesters, subject to limitations: paper photocopy 10 cents per page (single/double sided); 81/2 x 11 inch color copies 90 cents per page; color copies up to 11 x 17 inches $1.50 per page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For copies produced by computer and placed on an electronic device or provided as a printout, NCPC shall charge Direct Costs, including operator time. Other forms of duplication are charged their Direct Costs. No more than one paper copy shall be supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review fees for commercial use requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: Review fees shall be charged only to Requesters who make a Commercial Use Request for the NCPC initial review of a Record to determine whether an exemption applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No charge for review at the administrative appeal level for an exemption already applied. If a different exemption is applied on subsequent review, costs of that review are chargeable. Review fees charged at same rates as Search under paragraph (c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee limitations for untimely responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If NCPC fails to comply with FOIA time limits, NCPC shall not charge Search fees or (for Educational Institutions/Noncommercial Scientific Institutions/News Media) duplication fees, except as described in paragraphs (f)(2)–(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist for unusual circumstances with timely notice, court-ordered exceptional circumstances, and other statutory provisions as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unusual circumstances provision and additional time
rubrics_metrics.description: If NCPC determines unusual circumstances as defined by FOIA apply and provided timely written notice, a failure to comply with the time limit may be excused for an additional 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual circumstances are governed by FOIA definitions and procedural requirements for notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging when unusual circumstances and large volume exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If Unusual Circumstances exist and more than 5000 pages of responsive records are necessary, NCPC may charge Search fees and may charge duplication fees to Educational/Noncommercial/News Media requesters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies only if NCPC provides timely written notice of the Unusual Circumstances and makes at least three good faith efforts to discuss limiting the scope of the Request with the Requester via mail, email or phone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-ordered exceptional circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: If a court has determined that exceptional circumstances exist, a failure to comply with time limits shall be excused for the length of time provided by the court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows FOIA exceptional-circumstances rules as applied by courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum billing increment rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No Search or Review fees shall be charged for a quarter-hour period unless more than half of that period is required for Search or Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes rounding/threshold for charging partial quarter-hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free search and duplication allowances for non-commercial requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for Commercial Use Requesters, NCPC shall provide without charge the first two hours of Search (or cost equivalent) and the first 100 pages of Duplication (or cost equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a per-request allowance before charging fees to non-commercial requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis fee threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for Commercial Use Requesters, no fee shall be charged for a Request if the total fee calculated under this section equals $50.00 or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests costing $50 or less are not charged to qualifying requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for charging non-commercial requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters other than Commercial Use Requesters shall not be charged a fee unless the total cost of a Search in excess of two hours plus Duplication in excess of 100 pages totals more than $50.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines free allowances and de minimis threshold into charging trigger for non-commercial requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when estimated fees exceed $50 and suspension of processing
rubrics_metrics.description: If NCPC determines or estimates fees in excess of $50.00, NCPC shall notify the Requester of the actual or estimated amount of total fees; the Request shall not be considered received for purposes of timeframes and no further work undertaken until the Requester agrees to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only a portion of the fee can be estimated, NCPC shall advise that the estimate is partial. Any agreement to pay must be memorialized in writing. Notice should offer opportunity to reformulate the Request to lower cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special service charges
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Requester asks for, or NCPC chooses to provide as administrative discretion, special service (e.g., certifying records are true copies or sending by other than ordinary mail), the actual costs of the special service shall be charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special services are charged separate from standard search/duplication fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest and debt collection on unpaid fees
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall charge interest on any unpaid fee starting on the 31st day following the date of billing at the rate provided in 31 U.S.C. 3717; NCPC shall follow provisions of the Debt Collection Act of 1982.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest accrues from billing date until payment; collection may use consumer reporting agencies, collection agencies, and offset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of requests to prevent fee avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where NCPC reasonably believes multiple Requesters are acting in concert to subdivide a Request to avoid fees, NCPC may aggregate the Requests and charge accordingly; presumes multiple requests within 30 days made to avoid fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests separated by more than 30 days may be aggregated if a solid basis exists under all circumstances involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance payment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC generally shall not require an advance payment except: when estimated total fee exceeds $250 (NCPC may require all or part advance payment), or where Requester previously failed to pay properly charged FOIA fee within 30 days (NCPC shall require payment of past due plus advance payment of anticipated fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advance payment required, Request shall not be considered received and no further work will be undertaken until payment is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to other agencies with statutory fee schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Records responsive to Requests are maintained for distribution by Agencies operating statutorily-based fee schedule programs, NCPC shall inform Requesters of steps for obtaining Records from those sources so they may do so most economically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC should guide requesters to the most cost-effective source for records when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: All fees shall be paid by personal check, money order or bank draft drawn on a bank of the United States, payable to the Treasurer of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable forms of payment for FOIA fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waiver public-interest standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Records shall be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge if the Requester demonstrates and NCPC determines disclosure is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government operations or activities and disclosure is not primarily in the Requester’s commercial interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC must determine based on all available information whether both prongs (public interest contribution and non-commerciality) are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for public-interest determination
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine if disclosure is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding, NCPC shall consider: whether subject concerns identifiable government operations or activities (direct/clear connection); whether disclosure would be meaningfully informative and not duplicative; whether it will contribute to understanding of a reasonably broad audience (requester’s expertise to convey considered; news media presumed to satisfy); and whether disclosure will enhance public understanding significantly compared to prior knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC shall not make value judgments about importance; information already in public domain or duplicative is not likely to contribute. Representatives of the News Media are ordinarily presumed to satisfy the public interest standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for assessing whether disclosure is primarily commercial
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall consider whether the Requester has a commercial interest that would be furthered by disclosure, and whether any identified commercial interest is sufficiently large compared to the public interest in disclosure that disclosure is primarily commercial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters shall be given an opportunity to provide explanatory information. NCPC ordinarily presumes Representatives of the News Media satisfy the public interest standard; disclosure to data brokers or those who compile and market government information for direct economic return shall not be presumed to primarily serve the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial fee waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where only some Records to be released satisfy Fee Waiver requirements, a Fee Waiver shall be granted for those Records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for Fee Waiver should address factors in paragraphs (a)-(c); NCPC may consider cost-effectiveness of administrative resources in deciding to grant waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of FOIA correspondence and provided Records
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall preserve all correspondence pertaining to FOIA Requests received and copies or Records provided until disposition or destruction is authorized by NCPC’s General Records Schedule or NARA-approved schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures recordkeeping until formal disposition authority is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-destruction of responsive materials while requests or litigation pending
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials responsive to a FOIA Request shall not be disposed of or destroyed while the Request or a related lawsuit is pending even if otherwise authorized for disposition under schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects against destruction during pending administrative or judicial matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of key Privacy Act terms (Adverse Determination, IIF, Record, System of Records, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of defined terms used throughout the Privacy Act rules, including: Adverse Determination (decisions to withhold, nonexistence, non-amendment, denial of accounting or fee waiver, or adequacy of search), Information in Identifiable Form (IIF), Record, Requester, Request for Access, Routine Use, SAOP, SORN, Workday, PIA, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provide the operative meanings used for applying the Privacy Act rules and procedures; e.g., IIF includes direct identifiers and indirect identification by combinations of data elements; Record includes items about an Individual maintained by NCPC with an identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and responsibilities of Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall designate a SAOP to establish and oversee the Privacy Act Program and ensure compliance; responsibilities include reporting to OMB and Congress on SORs, signing Privacy Act SORNs, approving and signing PIAs, and serving as head of the breach response team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAOP is the senior official accountable for agency privacy program functions and external reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and responsibilities of Privacy Act Officer (PAO)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall designate a Privacy Act Officer to coordinate and implement the Privacy Act program; responsibilities include developing policies, maintaining program records, responding to Privacy Act requests and appeals, informing individuals of disclosures, assisting with SORNs and PIAs, preparing reports to OMB, and evaluating PIAs for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAO handles day-to-day operational implementation of Privacy Act duties and coordination with divisions and legal/process owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division Directors' Privacy responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC Division Directors shall coordinate with the PAO to implement System of Records requirements applicable to their management area and the preparation of PIAs prior to development or procurement of systems that collect IIF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific duties include reviewing existing SORs for need/relevance/accuracy, coordinating SORN and PIA preparation, collecting information directly from individuals when possible, amending Records when appropriate, ensuring system use only for stated purpose, and establishing safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: CIO responsibilities for privacy and IT security
rubrics_metrics.description: The CIO shall implement IT security management including security for information protected by the Privacy Act and the E-Government Act; responsibilities include overseeing security policy for privacy data and reviewing PIAs for information security considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIO ensures technical security posture and integration with privacy assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: System developers/designers' responsibility for privacy-by-design
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC System Developers and Designers shall ensure IT system design and specifications conform to privacy standards and requirements and that technical controls are in place to safeguard personal information from unauthorized access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires incorporation of technical controls and privacy compliance into system development lifecycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configuration Control Board (CCB) PIA verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The NCPC CCB shall verify that a PIA has been prepared prior to approving a request to develop or procure IT that collects, maintains, or disseminates Information in Identifiable Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CCB acts as gatekeeper to ensure PIAs are completed before IT procurement/development approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee and Chairman responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC employees must protect personal information in accordance with rules; the Chairman of the Commission shall act on appeals of Adverse Determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns responsibilities across staff and leadership for compliance and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for content and quality of Records
rubrics_metrics.description: Records maintained shall contain only information relevant and necessary to accomplish a purpose NCPC must accomplish; Records used to make determinations about individuals shall be accurate, relevant, timely, and complete to assure a fair determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes limitations on scope of data collection and quality assurances when Records affect rights/benefits/privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for direct collection from Individual and practicability factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Information used to make determinations about an Individual’s rights/benefits shall be collected, to greatest extent practicable, directly from the Individual; NCPC shall consider whether information can only be obtained from third party, comparative cost, risk of inaccuracy from third parties, whether verification is required, and whether the Individual can verify third-party information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides five factors (1–5) to assess practicability of direct collection versus third-party collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on maintaining First Amendment activity records
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall not Maintain Records describing how an Individual exercises First Amendment rights unless maintenance is expressly authorized by statute, by the Individual, or is pertinent to and within scope of an authorized law enforcement activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects records of expressive activity unless narrowly authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements when collecting information from individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Individual asked to supply information for addition to a System of Records shall be informed of the basis for requesting the information, its potential use, and consequences of not supplying it; minimum notice must state legal authority and whether disclosure is mandatory or voluntary; principal purposes; potential routine uses as published in SORN; and effects of not providing requested information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice may be provided on the form, on an attached tear-off sheet, or on a separate form; NCPC may ask individuals to acknowledge receipt of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: System of Records Notice (SORN) publication and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall publish a notice in the Federal Register describing each System of Records 40 days prior to establishing a new or revised System; SORN must include name/location, categories of individuals, categories of Records, statutory authority, purposes and routine uses, policies/practices regarding storage/retrieval/access/retention/disposal, responsible official, notification procedures for individuals, and sources of Records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SORN content requirements are exhaustive to ensure transparency and public comment opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to safeguard Records (administrative, technical, physical)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall implement procedures to ensure sufficient administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect security and confidentiality of Records and protect against anticipated threats/hazards that could cause substantial harm, embarrassment, inconvenience, or unfairness to any Individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual Records must be maintained commensurate with sensitivity and minimum safeguards (or comparable protection) shall apply to manual Systems of Records.
